name: Animated Reaction Captions
visualIdentity: Concise emphasis captions use expressive display lettering, consistent layered outlines and shadows, reaction stickers, and small doodles. Emotions have distinct colors and motion; this is a broadcast reaction-text treatment, not continuous subtitles or general kinetic typography.
suitableUses: Best for short reactions and verbal emphasis in videos, or as a real-text overlay in interactive HTML. Music-backed shorts and highlight reels with few spoken lines suit beat-cued pops. 9:16 is an optional example, not a requirement.
limitations: Keep faces, dialogue subtitles, and platform overlays unobstructed. Hold captions long enough to read; reading holds take priority over beat density. Avoid popping on every beat or adding beat-reactive colors. Three emotion treatments and 9:16 framing are optional examples.
palette: Optional new-artwork suggestion: background #FFF5E5, foreground #282E3B, emotion accents #DA855C, #668FA3, and #A47CA3, assigned consistently. Supplied, brand, reference, semantic, and asset colors take precedence; preserve exact values and roles. Use discrete colors, no added gradient. #668FA3 and #A47CA3 are decorative fills, not normal text backings with the suggested foreground. Check contrast on actual composited frames.
motionAndInteraction: Use short spring entrances, squash, bounce, and wobble timed to reactions or verbal stress, then provide readable holds. For video, derive state from shared seekable time and verify direct, backward, and repeated seeks. HTML may sync to media time; hover, scroll, or pointer behavior is only for interactive delivery. Respect reduced motion and preserve the style cadence.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or audio layer is required. Choose music, voiceover, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and audience; honor supplied assets and directions. Beat-lock only when a supplied soundtrack drives reactions, leaving room for speech and comprehension. Check intelligibility, balance, clipping, and sync.
assetRequirements: Use actual fonts and SVG strokes or aligned text copies for outlines and shadows; group text and stickers as reusable components. Load local fonts and assets. Rough.js is optional for seeded doodles, not handwriting or character posing. Keep text as real text for HTML overlays.
combinations: Usually works best alone. Optional style-105 beat timing can cue entrances to a supplied soundtrack, while retaining emotion colors, phrase-length holds, safe areas, and no bounce under reduced motion. Avoid when beat density would compromise reading.
productionApproach: Select style renderer and motion engine for the artwork and action; assign each animated property one owner and expose deterministic time-based output. HTML/CSS and SVG are core options; PixiJS, Rough.js, Motion, and mo.js are optional role-specific tools. HyperFrames handles assembly, timing, sync, validation, and export by default; use Remotion only for a verified HyperFrames limitation or unavailability. For interactive HTML, wire behavior to media time or user input as appropriate.
